(d) and (e) There is no specific study regarding eradication of T.B. However, the National 
T.B. Control Programme was reviewed by a team of national and international experts in 1992. 
Based on their recommendations, Government of India evolved a revised programme, 
RNTCP, which was pilot tested in 1993, and expanded subsequently. In areas under RNTCP, 8 
out of 10 patients are being successfully treated compared to less than 4 out of 10 in the earlier 
programme and the death rate has been brought down 7 fold. A joint review of the RNTCP 
conducted in February, 2000 by Government of india and WHO has concluded that "RNTCP is

against the ban being lifted?

 There is no ban on manufacture of non-iodised salt except the restriction on

734. SHRIMATI CHANDRESH KUMARI: Will the Minister of HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have constituted some groups of women 
in the country since implementation of the Development of Women 
and Children in Rural Areas; 
 if so, details thereof with functions of the same; 
 whether Government propose to utilise these groups in other activities in case 
the objectives of DWCRA are achieved; and 
 if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI SUMITRA MAHAJAN): (a) and (b) The scheme for 
Development for Women and Children in Rural Areas (DWCRA) was in existence 
form 1982-83 to 1998-99 as a sub-scheme of Integrated Rural Development Programme 
(IRDP). From 1.4.1999, IRDP and its allied programme-including DWCRA were 
merged into the present self-employment programme i.e. Swarnjayanti Gram 
Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY). 
The primary objective of DWCRA was focussing attention on women members of 
the rural families below poverty line with a view to providing them opportunities of 
self-employment on a sustained basis. DWCRA thus focussed on providing income 
generating skill and activities to poor women in rural areas in order to improve their 
social and economic status. It also sought to encourage the. habit of thrift and credit 
among them. In addition, the programme aimed to enhance the welfare and quality of 
life of BPL family and community by improving the access of rural women to health, 
education, safe drinking wate r, sanitation, nutrition etc. A distinguishing feature of 
DWCRA was group strategy as against family as a unit of assistance under IRDP. The 
group strategy was adopted to motivate the rural women to come together and to break 
social bonds, which had denied them inco me generating and fulfilling opportunities. 
Each group comprised of about 10—-15 members which was provided a revolving   
fund   amounting   to   Rs.    15,000/-   upto   1994-95   and 
13_16GIPMR/2000 193

Rs. 25000/- from 1995-96. The fund was meant for the purpose of purchase of raw 
materials and marketing, honorarium to grou p organizer, infrastructure support for 
income generating and other group activities etc. The fund was shared equally by the 
Central Government and State Governments on 50-50 basis. In the case of Union 
Territories, Government of India provided cent per cent grant. (Prior to 1996-97, 
expenditure on Revolving Fund was shared between Central Government, State 
Government and UNICEF on 40:40:20 basis). 
Since inception upto 1998-99 a total of 2,72,722 groups were formed under 
DWCRA comprising 41,44,705 members. The central funds released to States/UTs 
during this period were Rs. 389,90 crore. 
(c) and (d) DWCRA groups of quality can be adopted in SGSY. The SGSY 
guidelines already provided for that. DRDAs have to put in concerted efforts to 
strengthen the groups formed under DWCRA during first year of SGSY.

THE MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRI T.R. BAALU) : Mr. 
Chairman, Sir, the Calling Attention motion on the death of animals in zoos and sanctuaries is 
evidence of the great empathy and concern that people in our country and Members of 
Parliament, in particular, have for wildlife. This will also send a clear and loud message to zoo 
and park managers that their performance is being closely watched by the nation and that their 
response to the mandate given to them has to be appropriate and adequate. Even before I 
received notice of this Calling Attention motion, I had proposed to seek leave to make a 
statement on the recent death of zoo tigers. 
I have personally monitored factors relating to the death of twelve tigers at 
Nandankanan 200. i have no reserv ation in admitting that th e zoo director and the zoo 
veterinarian were unable to show the professional competence that was expected of them. A 
number of significant inadequacies have been identified and the State Government has been 
requested to take mitigative measures. Overcrowding of anima !s, inappropriate housing, poor 
standards of sanitation and hygiene and inadequate expertise in the field of health care of zoo 
animals have jointly contributed to these deaths. Another negative factor has been the 
inadequate level of funding that the zoo has received from the State Government in the past 
years. 
Then I received information of some other upsetting incidents. The recent deaths of 
lions in Gir, cheetals in Ranthambore and peacocks at Morena were also enquired into. 
The information that I have is that except for one lion that was 
electrocuted, the death of the other lions was because of natural causes and currently there is 
no threat of any kind of infection to other animals in the area. As regards the death of cheetahs in 
Ranthambore, a few animals were killed by dogs in the fringe areas of the Park, whilst two 
animals were suffering from tuberculosis. ! will have something more to say on this later. in 
Morena district, investigations revealed that a number of peacocks died due to consumption of 
bajra seed which had been treated with pesticides. 
I would like to give some statistics about existing zoos. Presently, there are 199 
recognised zoos, of which 15 are large, 17 medium, 31 small 
245 

RAJYA SABHA [28 JULY, 2000)  
and 136 mini zoos and deer parks. The total number of animals in these zoos, which includes 
birds and reptiles, is around 25,000. Of this, 9000 animals belong to the endangered category. 
According to the information available with me, during the last four years, around 1600 animals 
have died in these zoos, which comes to about 10 per cent of the tola!. 
As regards tigers, their number in zoos is around 313. More than 75 per cent of the 
tigers are of captive-bred origin. No tiger has been captured in the last ten years for the purpose 
of display in the zoos. The number of tigers that have died between 1995-96 and 1998-99 is 141. 
Of this, tigers account for an average of 35 deaths in a year. This is about 12 per cent of the 
population of zoo tigers. The average birth rate of tigers during this period is about 19 per cent. 
As regards the number of wild animal deaths in sanctuaries approximately, 140 tigers, 
700 panthers, 450 elephants, 15 lions, and 127 rhinoceros have been killed by poachers in the 
last five years. 
In the wild, we have an estimated population of tigers, which is between 3500 and 
3700. Taking the average life span of tigers as 20 years, out of this population, not less than 176 
tigers would be dying of old age. There is the incidence of infant mortality also and about 400 
cubs die a natural death every year. Then, mere are instances of handicapped animals dying of 
starvation, as well as tigers killing each other to safeguard their territory. 
An area of concern that I would like to bring to the notice of the hon. Members is the 
negative impact of disturbances in the habitat of the animals and the inadequate prey base of the 
cats. This has resulted in a tendency on the part of tigers and other cats to increasingly look 
towards livestock to meet their food requirements. This has led to a man and animal conflict, with 
resultant instances of poisoning. 
The panther appears to be under greater threat because of its tendency to live in the 
fringe areas of the forest. Intrusions by panther into human habitation is not uncommon, where 
they are lured by easy prey availability of livestock: dogs and, at times, human infants. In this 
regard, the position tends to become quite grim at times in the hills of Himachal Pradesh and 
Uttar pradesh. There have also been instances of panther intrust ion into some  suburbs of 
Bombay and within the limits of Guwahati City.     Recently, in a series of seizures,  200 panther 
skins and a larger 
246 

[28 JULY, 2000] RAJYA SABHA 
number of other parts such as nails were seized. While the regulatory agencies have been put 
on the alert, these cases have been referred to the CBI. Separately, my Ministry is in the process 
of finalizing a proposal for an exclusive agency to investigate - wild life crimes. There are, 
however, other issues also. .We have made arrangements for increase in compensation for 
cattle deaths as also for speedy disbursement of compensation. Besides, a greater degree of 
awareness is also needed to sensitize those who are involved in man and animal conflicts about 
the precious loss to our biodiversity when needless senselessness takes place in such 
situations. My Ministry is working on a scheme to increase the level of public awareness in this 
area. 
I would like to mention that epidemics also take a heavy toll of wild animal life. 
Sometime around 1950, 30 to 40 per cent of the wild ass population was wiped out due to 
trypanosomiasis. In the seve nties, an outbreak of rinderpe st nearly wiped out the gaur 
population in Madumalai, parts of Periyar and Bandipur. Fortunately, nature has been able to 
revive the depleted population', assisted by availably of an adequate habitat and effective 
protection measures. 
Another important issue is the destruction of wild life habitats. Habitat destruction due 
to biotic pressures and various developmental activities have brought down the recruitment rate, 
especially in the case of the  tiger.      Sharing  of common  grazing   grounds  and  water  pool   
with 
livestock has brought in diseases like tuberculosis in national parks and sanctuaries. Cases of 
tuberculosis in tigers have been reported from Sariska in Rajasthan. 
Railway lines passing through forests continue to be a serious threat for elephants. 
Five elephants in Uttar Pradesh and six in Assam have died because of this reason. Road 
accidents have also taken a toll of wild animals in Kaziranga, Assam and Gir in Gujarat, 
I will be failing in my duty if ! do not mention that the draining of 
water bodies and swamps for agricultural purposes has severely affected the population of 
swamp deer and various species of water birds. Intensive agriculture and deforestation in high 
hill areas has intensified floods in our major rivers. The Kaziranga National Park is a regular 
victim of such floods. The Hoods in 1998 monsoons took a toll of two tigers, forty-four rhinos, 
247 

RAJYA SABHA [28 JULY, 2000]  
three elephants, three wild buffalos, fifty swamp deer and more than six hundred herbivores. 
There are reports of three elephants being washed away in flood waters in West Bengal, Use of 
pesticides has added another serious dimension to the problem. We are ail worried about fifty 
peacocks dying after eating bajra seeds coated with pesticide. I am informed that twelve 
elephants died in Dhenkanal district of Orissa because of consumption of agricultural crop 
which had been sprayed with pesticide by the farmers. Experience over the years has brought

research conducted in Andhra Pradesh says that there is a surplus of one lakh sixty thousand

Statement 
(a) and (b) It has been the constant endeavour of Doordarshan to modernise 
and upgrade its various facilities. Some of the specific projects commissioned/ 
completed by Doordarshan to modernise its facilities during 9th Plan are as follows:  
(i) New modern studios at Mumnai, Nagpur and Rajkot.  
(ii) Degital satellite uplink facilities for uplinking of its various channels such 
as DD-I, DD-II, DD-News, DD-Sports and DD-International.  
(iii) Simulcast uplinking facilities both in digital and analog at DDK Calcutta, 
Hyderabad, Trivandrum, Bangalore, Guwahati, Chennai and Mumbai.  
(iv) New automation facility at DDK, Delhi. 
In addition, state of the art equipment have Been provided to a number 
of Kendras and some old transmitters have also been replaced by new 
transmitters of higher power. 
(c) to (e) In the state of Orissa, Studio at Bhubaneswar equipped with 
modern 'equipment was commissioned during 8th Plan period and, thereafter, 
facilities at the station have been augmented from time to time. Additional studio 
equipment is envisaged to be provided Bhubaneswar studio, as part of 9th 
Plan,Besides, LPT at Baleshwar have been upgraded to 10 KW HPT, 10 KW 
HPT with 150 M tower is under installation at Sambalpur (inreplacement of 1 
KW transmitter) and a 1 KW transmitter at Berhampur (in replacement of 
present LPT). Also, the present LPTs Bargarh, Rajgangapur and Joda in Orissa 
are envisaged to be replaced by 500W Transmitters. 
Upgradation/replacement of 111 transmitters and 2 studios, besides various 
schemes relating to the provision of a dditional studio equipment, are under 
implementation in various parts of the country, including Orissa. State-wise

Flouting of Indecent Exposure of Women Act 
848. SHRI RAJNATH SINGH "SURYA": Will the Minister of 
INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware that the provisions of Indecent 
Exposure of Women Act are being flouted by print and visual media; 
(b) if so, the reasons for Government being unable to keep a watch 
and check it; 
(c) whether it is a fact that certain foreign-TV channels are doing it 
with impunity; and 
(d) if so, whether Government will put a ban on it? 
111 

RAJYA SABHA   [31st July, 2000] 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF INFORMATION AND 
BROADCASTING AND MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF LAW JUSTICE 
AND-COMPANY AFFAIRS (SHRI ARUN JAI TLEY): (a) to (d) A Doordarshan 
Broadcast Code already exists and all pr ogrammes telecast on Television by 
Doordarshan are governed by it. Doordarshan strictly abides by the provisions of 
Indecent Representation of Women Act, 1986, while telecasting its programmes. 
Doordarshan also follows the Code, which ensures that no advertisement has 
indecent, vulgar, suggestive, repulsive or offensive themes or treatment. The 
programmes of foreign satellite channels are uplinked from outside the country and, 
therefore, do not fall under the ambit of Indian laws; unless decoders are required 
for their reception. To bring the foreign satellite channels within the ambit of Indian 
laws, programme codes and standards, a comprehensive legislation is proposed for 
regulating private .< broa dcasting in the country. Cable Television Networks 
(Regulation) Act, 1995 is also proposed to be amended in order to achieve uniform 
applicability of Programme and Advertisement Codes on all satellite channels. 
All films, including advertisement films intended for public exhibition in India 
and required to be certified by the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) in 
accordance with the provisions of the Cinematograph Act, 1952 and the guidelines 
thereunder. CBFC, while examining films for certification, ensures, inter-alia, that 
human sensibilities are not offended by vu lgarity, obscenity, depravity, sex and 
violence. 
In so far as the Print Media is concerned, the Government does not interfere 
inmatters relating to the Press. The Press Council of India is a statutory authority 
established for preserving the freedom of the Press and for maintaining and 
improving the standards of newspapers and news agencies in India.

913. SHRIS. RAMACHANDRAN PILLAI: Will the Minister of 
URBAN DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the percentage of urban population living in slums in Delhi, 
Mumbai, Calcutta, Chennai, Ahmedabad, Hyderabad and other 
State capitals; and 
(b) the percentage of slum population enjoying facilities of tap 
water, proper sanitation, pucca Roads, health services, schools in 
slum areas in State Capitals, Capital-wise? 
THE MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY 
ALLEVIATION (SHRI JAGMOHAN): (a) There is no periodical 
assessment of slum population in India. However, the Town and 
Country Planning Organisation conducted a study and brought out 
a report entitled 'A Compendium on Indian Slums-1996'. 
Identified/estimated slum population of 23 metropolitan cities as 
given in the said report is enclosed (Annexure I in the Statement-I), 
this includes Delhi, Mumbai, Calcutta, Chennai Ahmedabad, 
Hyderabad, and a few State Capitals (See below). 
(b) Slum improvement is a State subject. Information regarding 
provision of water supply and sanitation facilities in the cities and 
towns is assessed on whole-town basis and not area-wise or 
category-wise. However based on the information received from the 
State PHE Departments, Water Boards etc., State-wise information in 
regard to. provision of drinking water supply facilities through House 
Service Connections.-Public St and Posts etc. and sanitation 
facilities provided through Sewerage, Low Cost Sanitation, septic 
tank etc. has been collected and  compiled. Accordingly, the 
percentage of population having access to drinking water supply 
facilities in urban areas has been assessed as about 90% and 
population provided with sewerage and sanitation facilities has been 
assessed as about 49% of the estimated urban population as on 
31.3.1997. The coverage percentage indicates accessibility only. It 
docs not indicate adequacy and equitable distribution of water 
supply as per the prescribed norms of Govt, of India. The State-wise 
coverage of urban population with water supply and sanitation 
facilities is given in Statement-II.

915, SHRI ANANTA SETHI; Will the Minister of URBAN

state: 
(a) whether Government have a pr oposal to privatise water 
supply in Delhi and other metropolitan cities; 
(b) if so, by when; and

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN  THE MINISTRY OF URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION (SHRI BANDARU 
DATTATRAYA): (a) to (c) The Ministry of Urban Development and 
Poverty Alleviation has no proposal to privatize water supply in 
Delhi and other metropolitan cities. Since this is a State subject, it 
is for the State Governments and metropolitan authorities to decide 
on this issue. The Ministry held a national seminar on Private Sector

As reported, the Delhi Jal Board, Chennai Metropolitan Water 
Supply and Sewerage Board, Calcutta Municipal Corporation and 
Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM) have no 
proposals to privatize water supply. However, MCGM is 
contemplating to award a management contract for management 
and distribution of water supply for one of its wards. 
The Government of Karnataka has a proposal to privatize water 
supply in Bangalore city since 1997. Bids received for the 
production and conveyance of 500 mld (million litres per day) of 
treated water to the city under the Cauvery Water Supply Scheme 
Stage-IV, Phase-II on BOOT. (Build-Operate-Own-Transfer) basis 
has been evaluated and negotiations held with the preferred bidder. 
Final decision to enter into an agreement is yet to take place. 
Government of Karnalaka/B an galore Water Supply and Sewerage 
Board has also proposed to take up delegated management 
contract in two pilot areas of the city for operation and maintenance 
of water supply and sewerage system, as well as construction of

(b) whether Government are thinking of developing secondary and 
tertiary towns for this purpose; and 
(c) the steps Government propose to take to tackle the problem of 
settlement of slum dwellers and whether there is any time-frame in this 
regard? 
THE MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY 
ALLEVIATION (SHRI JAGMOHAN): (a) T he Govt, is in the process of 
finalisation of a National Urban Policy which aims at promoting sustainable, 
efficient, well-managed, and regionally balanced urban development in the 
country. In the Policy, the emphasis is on rural urban continuum and an 
articulated human settlement system with a well-defined regional hierarchy 
that integrates and strengthens the urban centres and surrounding rural 
areas. The policy would also focus on strengthening local bodies, improving 
planning, management and urban governance, reducing poverty protecting 
environment, promoting healthy and af fordable housing as well as cost 
effective and efficient infrastruc ture; and services systems and thus 
improving the quality of life of urban inhabitants. 
(b)To encourage spatial dispersal of economic development and to 
increase ihc level of infrastructure and services and employment 
opportunities in medium and small towns at an accelerated pace, in order 
to promote growth in these towns so as to reduce migration to large cities 
and proliferation of slums this Ministry is already implementing such a 
scheme viz., Integrated Development of Small and Medium Towns 
(IDSMT). 
(c) The Problem of slum dwellers has been engaging attention of the 
Government since die Second Five Year Plan. At present following two 
specific schemes for the slum dwellers are going on:— 
(i)  Environment Improvement of Urban Slums (EIUS)—It is a Stale 
sector scheme. 
(ii) National Slum Development Programme (NSDP)—Under this 
programme additional Central assistance is being given to States/ 
UTs for (the development of urban slums. 
The problem of settlement of slum dwellers in urban areas is to be 
tackled within the overall framework of the Government's policies on a 
continuous basis. Therefore, no time frame has been fixed for this purpose.

feeding of the animal will not be less than 10 to 12 hours. If the particular parasite, 
Trypanosomia, is left in the meat, definitel y there is a chance of animals getting 
infected. But as per the scientists, this trypanosom parasite does not live beyond eight 
hours. So, food poisoning, or, infection through food, is ruled out.

COMMUNICATIONS (SHRI TAPAN SIKDAR): (a) Sir, the criteria 
for keeping a telephone in safe custody in MTNL is based on 
subscriber's request; depending upon the period of safe custody—(i) 
for safe custody period upto six months, full rental is being charged and 
telephone number as well as cable pair are kept reserved (ii) for safe 
custody period beyond six months 40% of the rental is being charged and 
telephone number and cable pair are not kept reserved.

custody if the telephone number and the cable pair are required to be kept 
reserved. 
 In case of a telephone under safe custody for a period beyond 
six months, where there is no specific request by the party to keep the 
telephone number & cable pair reserved on full rentals; the telephone 
number can be allotted to other party. 
 Yes, Sir.

the issuance of "Surrender Certificate" by MTNL, the party

high alert and vigilant to detect and prevent cross border smuggling of 
contraband goods.

other anti-India activities, States bordering Nepal have been advised 
to strengthen policing/patrolling and maintain strict vigil on the

l000. SHRI P.K. MAHESHWARI: Will the Minister of 
FINANCE be pleased to state:

regard to the charging of compound interest on the interest on loans 
taken by the farmers; 
 if so, the details thereof; 
 whether Government intend to charge simple interest instead 
of compound interest on such loans; 
 if so, the action taken in this regard alongwith the guidelines 
issued to the banks by Government; and 
 if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI BALASAHEB VIKHE PATIL): (a) to (e) No, Sir. Reserve 
Bank of India (RBI) has issued the following guidelines to commercial 
banks regarding the procedure for charging/ compounding interest on 
loan accounts: 
(i) In respect of direct agricultural advances, banks should not 
compound interest in case of current dues, i.e. crop loans and 
instalments not fallen due in respect of term loans, as the 
agriculturists do not have any regular source of income other 
than sale proceeds of their crops. When crop loans or 
instalments under term loans become overdue, banks can add 
interest outstanding to the principal; 
(ii) Further, total interest debite d to an account should not exceed   
the   principal   amount   in   respect   of  short-term 
advances to small and marginal farmers. 
RBI has also advised Commercial Banks that in the case of long 
duration crops like sugarcane etc. banks should charge interest at 
annual rates and compound the interest only if the loan/lnstalment 
becomes overdue.

Observations of CRISIL on Banking System 
1013. SHRI PARMESHWAR KUMAR AGARWALLA: Will 
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
 whether Government are aware of the observations of CRI 
SIL that the asset quality continues to  be the main handicap of Indian 
Banking system; 
 if so, what are the other observations made by CRISIL; and 
 what are Government's comments on the observations? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI BALASAHEB VIKHE PATIL): (a) In an analysis of the key 
risk factors impacting rating of  Indian Banks, the Credit Rating 
Information Services of India Limite d (CRISIL) have observed that it 
considers asset quality to be the main handicap of the Indian Banking 
system. 
 The same analysis while noting that Indian Banks still have a 
long way to go in upgrading credit risk management systems also 
takes note of the strengths of the sector such as a strong liquidity 
profile, limited vulnerability to external capital flows and the 
likelihood of support to public sector  banks arising from Government 
ownership. 
 Government as the owner or the majority shareholder and RBI 
as a regulator are confident that with the provisoning requirements 
being continuously tightened and ot her prudential norms being made 
more rigorous, as well as the increased awareness of the importance of 
an improved asset quality by the bank management's, the health of the 
Indian banking system is fundament ally sound. One significant aspect 
which should be noted is that in th e classification of assets the extent 
of provision is not netted out as is being done in other countries and 
hence figures of gross NPAs, whic h is often taken adverse note of, 
includes a significant component for which provisions are held by the 
banks.

is not taking measures to provide better equipments and machinery, like

changing trend of smuggling as well as  the economic scenario, Government 
has been taking effective steps to equip the field formations under the CBEC

detection of smuggling of contraband goods including narcotic drugs, 
explosives, arms and ammunitions, etc. At present, 105 nos..of Baggage X-

clearance of cargo & passengers. In addition, 4 nos. of Narcotics and 
Explosives Detectors (IDNSCAN Machines ) have recently been depolyed at 
4 major International Airports at Delhi, Mumbai, Calcutta & Chennai.

also been provided with 642 nos. of Hand Held Search Lights, 406 nos. of 
Simple Binoculars and 517 nos. of Night Vision Binoculars. Besides, 121

1028. SHRI V, P. DURAISAMY: Will the Minister of FINANCE 
be pleased to state: 
 whether India Development Forum which met in Paris for the 
first time after the Pokhran nuclear test in May 1998, did not pledge 
any fresh aid by donor countries led by the World Bank; 
 whether it is a fact that there was no fresh commitment 
indicating that the economic sanctions  imposed after the nuclear tests 
have not been fully lifted; and 
 what steps his Ministry will take to get assistance from them 
for poverty alleviation programmes and for effecting fiscal 
consolidation in the medium term both at the Centre and State? 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI YASHWANT SINHA); 
(a) Issues relating to sanctions and fresh commitments were not 
discussed at the India Development Forum Meeting held in May, 
2000. The agenda of the meeting fo cused on issues relating to 
effectiveness and relevance of external assistance in the framework of 
development planning in India and the need for structuring external 
aid to be consistent with the economic priorities of the country. The 
theme for discussion this year at the IDF was "Poverty-States 5 
Dimension". 
 No, Sir. Most of the major donors continue to make fresh 
commitments. The actual commitments made during 1999-2000 were 
USS 2093.66 million. 
 Most of the Donors/External agencies did not impose 
sanctions on programmes projects relating to Basic Human Needs, 
Hence, we continue to receive external assistance for poverty 
alleviation programmes. As per the 9th Plan document the total Met 
external assistance provides only 7% of the total plan investment. 
Fiscal consolidation is an ongoing process in the Ministry of Finance. 
For containing fiscal deficit, a number of measures have been initiated 
by the Ministry of Finance which include; setting up of a committee 
for examining the possibility of a strong institutional mechanism 
embodied in a Fiscal Responsibility Act, constitution of

1031. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: Will the Minister of LAW, 
JUSTICE AND COMPANY AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 whether pendency of all types of cases including those 
relating to litigation between two or more corporates is a cause of 
concern both for Government and the judiciary; 
 if so, whether any steps have been taken for the speedy 
disposal of such cases; and 
 if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF 
INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING AND MINISTER OF 
STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF LAW, JUSTICE AND COMPANY 
AFFAIRS (SHRI ARUN JAITLEY): (a) to (c) Pendency of all types of 
cases including those relating to corporate litigation between two or more 
corporates, is a cause of concern for both the Government and the 
Judiciary. Various steps have been taken by the Government for the 
speedy disposal of all cases. These include amendment in the Code of 
Civil Procedure and the Code of Criminal Procedure, increase in the 
number of posts of Judges/ Judicial Officers and adoption of alternative 
modes of dispute resolution, such as, arbitration and conciliation. Lok 
Adalats have been given a statutory base as supplementary forums for 
resolution of disputes. 
Steps taken by the Supreme Court of India and various High Courts 
to expedite disposal of cases include, inter alia, more practical 
categorisation and grouping of cases, non-accumulation of defective 
matters, setting up of specialised benches etc.

Hijacking of Italian merchant vessel 
1048. SHRI KRISHNA KUMAR BIRL A: Will the Minister of 
SURFACE TRANSPORT be pleased to state: 
 whether an Italian merchant vessel was recently hijacked on 
its way to Kandla Port in Gujarat; 
 if so, what are the details thereof; and 
 what action has been taken by Government to rescue the 
vessel from the hijackers? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
SURFACE TRANSPORT (SHRI HUKUMDEO NARAYAN 
YADAV): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) and (c) The Coast Guard Regional Headquarters, Mumbai 
received information from Chairman , Kandla Port Trust on 9th June, 
2000 that Merchant Vessel Medstar registered at Kings Town has 
reportedly been hijacked by 14 stowaways who had boarded the 
vessel at Port Bandar Abbas, Iran. The stowaways comprising 10 
Iranians and 04 Iraqis claimed to have bomb with them and 
threatened to blow the ship if th eir instructions were not followed. 
The ship after loading 312 MT of granite at Bandar Abbas was 
scheduled to arrive at Kandla Port on 11th June 2000. 
On 10th June, 2000 at about 2330 hrs the Master of the Ship 
reported that the vessel was 270 NM West of Okha and slowly 
heading towards East. The vessel wa s subsequently located by Coast 
Guard Ships at about 0230 hrs on 12th June approximately 70 NM 
due West of Okha well within the Indian EEZ. Thereafter, the vessel 
was kept under constant surveillance by the two CG Ships. The vessel 
remained adrift at the same position till a bout 1600 hrs on 12th June 
and escorted by CG Ships to Mumbai as per the request of the owners 
and the negotiators of the P&I Club in Germany, The vessel under CG 
escort arrived outer anchorage off Mumbai about 1930 hrs on 13th 
June, 2000 and remained under CG surveillance. The vessel was 
thereafter shifted to inner anchorage at about 1345 hrs on 14th June to 
facilitate boarding of the vessel by  investigating agencies. At about 
1620 hrs a bomb disposal squad of Mumbai Police and Joint 
Investigation   Team   (JIT)   comprising   representatives   of   Navy, 
189 

RAJYA SABHA [1 August, 2000] 
Customs, CBI and IB boarded the vessel and carried out the 
investigation onboard ship. The Commander, Coast Guard 
Region(West) provided assistance to the immigration authorities to 
carryout independent interrogati on. Representative from P&I Club, 
Bremen, Germany who arrived at Mu mbai alongwith an interpreter, 
also negotiated with the stowaways from 14—20 June, 2000. 
Consequently, the 10 Iranian stowaways were issued with travel 
documents by Iranian Embassy to travel by air and they left on 23rd 
June, 2000. The vessel sailed from Mumbai on 24th June with 04 Iraqi 
stowaways under escort of private security agencies hired by the 
owners of the vessel for Bandar Abbas via Kandla.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER 
RESOURCES    (SHRIMATI   BIJOYA    CHAKRAVARTY):    (a) 
Government of India has recognized the need for conservation and 
management of water resources. The utilisable surface water by conventional 
methods has been assessed as 690 BCM. To harness available water 
resources and augment water supplies, ab out 3600 large dams and reservoirs 
and 250 barrages have been constructed. A total live storage capacity of 
about 177 BCM has been provided by 1995. An additional live storage 
capacity of about 75 BCM will be created on completion of the dams, which 
are under various stages of construction. Proposals to take up additional dams

formulation/consideration. The replenishable groundwater resources are of 
the order of 432 BCM out of which about 154 BCM has been developed for 
use.

Development Projects are planned and constructed by the State Government 
according to their priority  with their own resources . Government of India 
under "Accelerated Irriga tion Benefits Programme (ABP)" is providing 
Central Loan Assistance to State Governments for expeditious completion of 
ongoing multipurpose projects and completion of other medium and minor 
projects which are in the advanced stage of construction. Besides, the 
Government of India is also promoting Rainwater harvesting through

in the country include:—

control of ground water management and development.

Recent Incidents of Bomb Blasts in Various Paris Of The Country And Action 
Taken by Government 
SHRI EDUARDO FALEIRO (Goa) : Mr. Chairman, Sir. I call the 
attention of the Minister of Home Affairs to the recent incidents of bomb blasts 
in various parts of the country and action taken by the Government in that 
regard. 
THE MINSITER OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRI L.K. ADVANI) : The 
major concerns of the internal security scenario in the country centre around 
Pak-sponsored terrorism in Jammu & Kashmir, inter-linked and externally 
supported subversive activities of militant groups in the North-East and the 
violence perpetrated by the Left-Wing extremist groups in some States. 
Resort to the use of bombs and Improvised Explosive Devices (IED) by 
various militant and extremist groups has remained a regular feature in recent 
years. The targets in these incident s of explosions have been innocent 
people, selected VIPs, important polit ical leaders and Security Force 
personnel. In Jammu & Kashmir, militants have come to notice using 
sophisticated explosive devices and causing damage to life and property. Use 
of explosives for causing blasts in trains by various terrorist and insurgent groups 
in some parts of the country have also been reported. The Left-Wing 
extremist groups in Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar have also 
been using lEDs. They have also come to notice stockpiling explosives for use 
during elections. 
A series of bomb blasts had also occurred in church premises in 
the States of Goa, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka in the mouths of June and 
July. The investigations carried out by the Central Agencies and the police 
forces of the three States have revealed that a group known as Deendar 
Anjuman having their links in Pakistan, is involved in the incidents with the aim 
to create differences between various communities. Nine culprits are reported 
to have been arrested so far. Further investigations are going on.

•141. SHRIMATI VANGA GEETHA: Will the Minister of HOME  AFFARIS be pleased to 
state:

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRI 
CHENNAMANENI VIDYA SAGAR RAO): (a) 
to (c) A statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
The Law Commission of India has submitted its 173rd report on Prevention of Terrorism Bill, 
2000. According to the Law Commission the draft bill seeks to provide Law enforcement agencies 
with suitable powers to deal effectively with the growing menace of terrorism in the country and 
also contains provisions for checking misuse of powers by the investigating agencies. 
The salient features of the Bill include a comprehensive definition of terrorist acts, provisions 
for seizure, attachment and forfeiture of proceeds of terrorism; provisions for expeditious trial by 
special courts and protection of witnesses; inve stigation by office not below the rank of Deputy 
Superintendent of Police or equivalent as also adverse inference as to accused in certain cases. 
Suitable safeguards against abuse of various provisions have been provided including confirmation 
of detention by Director General of Police an d State Review Committees within ten and thirty 
days respectively, etc. 
The Government has invited the views of the all the State Government/UT administrations on 
the various provisions of the bill. The Government will hold consultations with political parties 
and other concerned agencies/groups before taking a final view.

(a) whether it is a fact that the Solar Energy Programme is regarded- as one of the World's 
largest programme, if so, the countries which; are following the similar kind of programmes; 
(b) what 'are the highlights of the Solar Energy Programme in other countries;  
(c) if the programme. is commercially viable in  other countries, what, is the.cost incurred 
thereon; and 
(d.) what is: the difference in the level of technologies used in India and other countries? 
134 

 137
 [2 August, 2000] RAJYA SABHA 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF NON-CONVENTIONAL  ENERGY 
SOURCES (SHRI M. KANNAPPAN): (a) and (b) Th e Indian "solar energy programme is 
regarded as one of the largest national programmes in the world in this field. Other, countries 
which have policies to support solar energy deve lopment as well as major programmes in solar 
photovoltaic and thermal technologies  include USA, Japan, Germany,  China, Australia, France, 
Netherlands, Austria, Israel, Italy and Spain. 
USA is pursuing the development and utilization of a variety of solar technologies for a large 
number of applications. A programme for the installation of 1 miltidtt solar systems on roof-tops 
of houses and Other buildings was announced in 1997. This includes solar photovoltaic systems 
for electricity generation as well as solar thermal systems for water heating. In Germany, a new 
programme for 100,000 solar roofs was launche d in 1999. About 33,000 roof-top photovoltaic; 
systems have been installed in Japan till March 2000 under its national programme. In Israel, 
legislation has made it mandatory to install sola r water heaters in several types of buildings 
including most residential utitis. Megawatt- size power plants based on solar thermal and 
photovoltaic technologies have been installed in USA. Photovotaic power plants have also been 
installed for purposes of demonstration and evalua tion in several other countries including Italy, 
Germany and Japan, Research and development is also being suppor ted in Japan, USA,.Australia 
and several European countries. 
(c) The commercial viability of any solar energy system depends on a number of factors such as 
the solar radiation level, load, c onsumption pattern and the availabili ty and cost of electricity or 
fossil fuels. The cost of electricity from solar thermal or photovoltaic sy stems is generally not 
competitive to that: generated from conventional energy sources. The megawatt-size power plants 
abroad have been built either under government-funded demonstration programmes or by 
availing of special tax benefits and other ince ntives. The solar roof programme in Japan is 
supported by government subsidies; in Germany it is supported by soft loans.and a special price 
for the electricity supplied to the grid by hous e owners. The international price for photovoltaic 
modules is around $ 4 per watt and the cost of electricity for stand-alone systems varies between 
135 

 138
RAJYA SABHA [2 August, 2000] 
25 to 50 cents per kilowatt hour. However, photo voltaic power can be economical in remote and 
unelectrified areas and for small power applications, as is also the case in India. 
Solar water heating systems for household use are c onsidered to be commercially viable in most 
countries including India. The cost of a solar water hearing system of 100—120 litre capacity 
varies between $ 400—600. Industrial and institutional solar water heating systems are 
competitive only if the alternative is electricity or a high-priced fuel. 
(d) As a result of development and commercialisation efforts made during the past two decades, a 
substantial base for the manufac ture of solar photovoltaic and solar thermal products has been 
established in India. Almost the entire production of solar cells in India is based on the single 
crystal silicon technology. Technologies such  as multi-crystalline silicon, amorphous silicon and 
other thin film solar cells which account for over 60% of the world's production are not yet in 
commercial production in India. Nevertheless, so lar cells and modules made in India are being 
exported to several countries abroad. Solar collector material for thermal applications is also being 
exported from India. Several Indian companies have obtained the ISO 9000 quality certification. 
The main difference in the production of solar pr oducts in India and some other countries lies in 
the volume of production and the range of techno logies employed. Lead ing foreign companies 
have production capacities which ar e 5 to 10 times that of Indian companies. A higher level of 
automation is also seen in foreign manufacturing organizations.

Compensation to Kuwait Evacuees 
SHRI C. RAMACHANDRAIAH (Andhra Pradesh): Sir, during the Iraq-Kuwait war, thousands of 
Indians working in Kuwait were evacuated. Ther eafter, a United Nations Claims Commission 
was established at Geneva to compensate the vi ctims who lost their earnings and savings due to 
the war. The victims were asked to send their claims for compensation to the United Nations 
Claims Commission (UNCC) through their respec tive Governments. In India, the Special 
Kuwait Cell coordinated and monitored the pro cessing of applications and disbursement of 
compensation. Accordingly, the Government of India, as per the decision of the UNCC, received 
applications for claims until 1991 and extended the time thereafter upto 1992. Corresponding to 
these dates, the victims had sent their applications. The Government of India notified a proforma 
in newspapers for submitting their claims. Howeve r, most of the victims of the evacuation are 
illiterate labourers and not well educated and they  could not have read the newspapers. Hence, 
they were not aware of the new procedures that have been adopted and they could not send their 
applications in the new proforma. However, the applications which were sent in plain papers 
were rejected and the victims were denied the compensation with the sole reason that they failed 
to apply in the appropriate format. All th ese victims are sufferi ng from utter poverty and 
unemployment. They are not even able to meet their needs and have two meals a day. Sir, 
thousands of workers from my district, Cuddapah,  in Andhra Pradesh are being denied of this 
compensation amount. They are unable to come over to Delhi and stay here for some days for 
this purpose. It is a costly affair to them; he nce most of the people could not come. However, 
even in the case of those people who managed to come over here, the Kuwaiti Embassy officials 
are not even giving appointments to them as their names are not included in the list of eligible 
persons for receiving the compensation. Consider ing this miserable condi tion of the people, I 
request the Government to consider their applications sympathetically and grant the 
compensation which is legitimately due to them.

Before replying to the specific points raised by  the Members of Parliament, I would like to give 
some background to the repeal of these two laws. 
The Department of Administrative Reforms had set up a Commission under the chairmanship of 
Shri P.C. Jain, in May, 1998, to review the laws and regulations, id entifying proposals for 
amendments to the existing laws and to make recommendations for repeal/amendment of the 
laws. 
The Commission has identified certain laws which are no longer relevant and, therefore, can be 
repealed. For the steel sector, the laws identified are: 
(1) The Iron & Steel Company (Taking over of Management) Act, 1972. 
(2) The Iron & Steel Companies (Amalgamation) Act, 1952. 
The Iron and Steel Companies (Amalgamation) Act, 1952 (Act No.79 of 1952) was enacted to 
amalgamate the Indian Iron & Steel Company Limited with the Steel Corporation of Bengal on 
the recommendation of the Tariff 
245 

 
RAJYA SABHA      [02 August, 2000] 
Board and the Tariff Commission. In the initia l years, after independence, when a serious 
shortage of steel was hampering the nation-building activities, it became imperative to eliminate 
duplication and waste and, ultimately, reduce the co st of production of steel. For this purpose, it 
was thought fit that the Stee! Corporation of Be ngal Limited, which had its works at Kulti, 
District Burdwan, West Bengal and the Indi an Iron and Steel Company Limited, Burnpur, 
District Burdwan, West Bengal, both of which were enga ged in the manufacture and production 
of iron and steel, should be amalgamated. The amalgamation was thought necessary to give effect 
to the schemes of the Centra! Government for expansion of the iron and steel industry and to 
make resources available for such expansion. 
The Act has now served its purpose, and no action might have been left over, which has to be 
undertaken under or in accordance with the provisions  of the said Act. It is, therefore, no more 
necessary to retain this Act on the Statute Book. 
Secondly, in accordance with the previsions of  the Indian Iron and Steel Company (Taking over 
of Management) Act, 1972 the ma nagement of Indian Iron and Steel Company was taken over 
initially for a period of two years, w.e.f. 14.7.1972, to secure its proper management. The period 
was extended for five years to co mplete restructuring and to streamline the administrative set-up 
of the Company. The said period of five years expired on 15 ,h July, 1977. Consequently, the Act 
is no longer operative. Subsequently, the Indian Iron and Steel Company (Acquisition of Shares) 
Act, 1976 was passed and the company was completely nationalised. In 1978, IISCO became a 
subsidiary of SAIL under the Public Sector iron and Steel Copmpanies (Restructuring) and 
Miscellaneous Act of 1978. Thus,. the Act, having  seized its purpose, is no longer operative and 
can be removed from the Statute book.

connected with the restructuring of SAIL or w ith the proposed conversion of IISCO into a joint

accounted for 70% of our population, In the last 50 years, because of occupational 
diversification, the share of agriculture in the national income of our country has gone down 
from 50% to 28%. But the share of agricultural population in the lotal population has come down

STATEMENT BY MINISTER 
Incidence of killing by the Militants in Jammu and Kashmir on the intervening night of 1st 
and 2nd August, 2000 
THE MINISTER OF HOME AFFAIRS {SHRI L.K. ADVANI): Madam, a series of ghastly 
incidents perpetrated by militants, taking a toll of  as many as 80 lives,  have been reported from 
Jammu and Kashmir on the 
night of r: and 2'''' August, 2000. 
In the first incident, at about 18-45 hours on 1 SI August, a group of terrorists fired 
indiscriminately at Pahalgam where Amarnath Ya tris were camping. The incident took place 
across Lidder Nallah on the road leading to Aroo when terrorists fired at two Langars and CRPF 
personnel. The firing was retaliated by the CRP F. 27 persons, including two police personnel, 
have been killed and 50 injured. Two militants re sponsible for the firing were also killed on the 
spot. From them, the following recoveries have been effected: AK Rifles-2, AK Magazines- 19, 
Rifie grenades--8, Hand-grenades--2, Grenade launcher-1, Rounds-55, Transistor--1.

RAJYA SABHA      [02 August, 2000] 
In the second and third incidents, the militants had attacked two brick ki ln labour camps, one at 
Mir Bazar, Quazigund in Anantnag District, the other at Mir Nowgam (Achhabal). 19 labourers 
were killed at Mir Bazar and 7 labourers at Mir Nowgam. During the same night, in Pogal 
Paristan in Ramban area (Doda District), anot her group of militants killed 14 persons. In the 
same district in village Keyar, eight members of a village defence committee were killed by 
terrorists. The sixth incident took place at Kalaroos (Kupwara district) where five members of a 
Muslim family were massacred. 
The Stale Government has initiated precautionary and relief measures. Special Secretary in the 
Department of J and K Affairs,  along with DG, CRPF have been deputed to J and K to review 
the situation and the security arrangements along with the security forces in the field. 
Consequent on the cease-fire declaration made by the Hizbul Muzahideen and the Government's 
positive response to this offer, th ere have been reports that some of the other militant outfits, 
with a large component of foreign mercenaries,  who were unhappy about the offer of Hizbul 
Mujahideen, may create problems and escalate violence. The security forces had been alerted of 
this and have been asked to be more vigilant. II is because of this vigilance that the security 
forces had foiled an atternpt of the militants to attack the Amarnath pilgrims in a Jammu camp 
on the morning of 1st August. In this clash, one militant was killed and another injured. 
No words would be too strong to condemn these outrageous incidents of violence which are no 
doubt part of the continuing proxy war being wa ged against us by a hostile neighbour. But the 
Government feels that this latest  outburst of violence is also a determined bid by those upset at 
the prospects of peace to abort the initiative taken by the Hizbul Mujahideen last week. 
The Government is determined to continue the Amarnath Yatra with renewed security measures 
and to provide all necessary protection to the common people. Besides, the Government will 
persevere in its efforts to bring normalcy to th e State of Jammu and Ka shmir by engaging in a 
dialogue with the peace-loving people.
